pages.summary: The page gives a solid high-level orientation to what the product is and why it exists, but stops well short of what a decision-maker needs to make a go/no-go call — specifically, there are no production readiness signals, no support tier details, and no TCO or sizing anchors on this page.
gaps: No GA vs. Tech Preview status is stated anywhere on the page, which is the first thing I need before I can assess production readiness or adoption risk.
Commercial support is referenced but not described — no SLA tiers, support scope, or pricing signals are surfaced, leaving TCO and risk coverage unresolvable from this page alone.

pages.summary: This page gives a clear enough high-level orientation to VMO's purpose and deployment options to support an initial evaluation framing, but it stops well short of what a decision-maker needs to assess production readiness, support tiers, licensing costs, or compliance posture before approving next steps.
gaps: There is no mention of GA vs. Tech Preview status, support tier, or known limitations for either deployment approach — the single most important signal for a go/no-go evaluation is absent.

TCO indicators are missing entirely: no licensing model, no sizing guidance, and no integration effort estimates are provided, making it impossible to estimate total cost of ownership or time-to-value from this page alone.

pages.summary: This landing page is purely navigational marketing copy with no actionable prerequisites, required inputs, or setup steps — a platform engineer cannot accomplish any concrete task from this page alone.
gaps: No prerequisites checklist, required permissions, network requirements, or version matrix are present anywhere on the page — the page provides zero technical content to act on.
The only concrete next step offered is "book a demo," which is a sales motion, not a self-service onboarding path for someone ready to stand up infrastructure.

pages.summary: The page outlines the correct high-level sequence and prerequisites clearly, but critical mid-sequence steps (TUI configuration, network/bond setup in Local UI, storage configuration, content bundle upload via CLI, and cluster deployment) are truncated or missing from the provided content, leaving the actual execution path incomplete.
gaps: The step-by-step content for "Configure the Node with the Palette TUI," "Configure the Network in Local UI," "Create a Bond," "Configure the Storage," "Upload the Content Bundle," and "Deploy the Cluster" sections are entirely absent from the rendered content — the page TOC lists them but the body text cuts off mid-sentence after the OS install step, making it impossible to execute the core installation sequence without navigating to sections not included here.

The prerequisites reference multiple external pages (Hardware Requirements, Certified Models by Hardware, Installation Architecture, Known Issues) for critical inputs like VIP/platform IP constraints, GPU memory ceilings, and BIOS setting names, but none of that content is provided, so I cannot validate whether my environment meets requirements before starting.

pages.summary: This page clearly explains what IAM roles and policies Palette auto-creates per cluster type, and flags the critical 10-policy limit, but it stops short of providing the actual policy documents or ARNs needed to configure the connecting IAM User/Role before deployment begins.
gaps: The page references "Core IAM Policies" and "Minimum Permissions Policies" (including dynamic vs. static variants) as the two options for granting Palette access, but provides zero policy JSON, ARNs, or attachment steps — you're forced to navigate away before you can do anything concrete.
There is no prerequisite checklist or required-permissions list for the IAM User/Role used to *register* the AWS account with Palette, which is the actual Day-0 task this page implies it covers.

pages.summary: The page gives a clear hardware/model compatibility matrix that helps narrow GPU procurement decisions, but it leaves critical production-readiness and licensing signals completely unaddressed, which blocks a go/no-go evaluation.
gaps: There is no indication of GA vs. Tech Preview status for any of the certified models or the Inference Launchpad itself, which is the first thing I need before assessing adoption risk.

The page provides no TCO signals — no licensing implications for certified vs. bring-your-own models, no support tier differences between certified and uncertified configurations, and no clarity on what "contact Spectro Cloud" means in terms of cost or timeline for custom certification requests.

pages.summary: The page gives a reasonable high-level orientation to Palette's deployment models and data flow, which is useful for initial scoping, but it leaves critical evaluation gaps around production readiness signals, support tiers, and compliance posture that a go/no-go decision requires.
gaps: There is no indication of GA vs. Tech Preview status, support tier, or SLA commitments for any of the three deployment models, which are the first things I need before assessing adoption risk.

The page references a separate "Security section" for compliance and security posture details but provides no summary or direct link, leaving a key vendor evaluation criterion completely unaddressed on this page.

pages.summary: The page gives me enough to pick an install method and size my deployment, but it stops short of the actual prerequisites checklist and dependency order I need before touching any install guide.
gaps: No explicit prerequisites section (required permissions, network CIDRs, firewall rules beyond the proxy domain table, or credential inputs) before I can confidently start any install path — the proxy/domain table covers egress but says nothing about inbound ports, vCenter permissions, or IAM requirements.

The Kubernetes version matrix splits across three tabs (VMware, Kubernetes, Management Appliance) but the page content truncates mid-table and never clarifies whether "non-EOL up to the specified version" means I can use, for example, 1.35.x on a Helm install targeting Palette 4.9.38 — leaving the exact supported floor version undefined.

pages.summary: This index page gives me a clear map of Day-2 operational tasks I care about, but it's a pure navigation page with zero procedural content — I can orient myself but cannot execute anything from it alone.
gaps: No indication of which guides have preconditions or dependencies (e.g., does "Upgrade the Platform" require a maintenance window, quorum check, or rollback path before I click anything?).

Missing any signal about SLO/health-validation steps post-action — none of the guide summaries mention expected outputs, success criteria, or failure indicators that would tell me if an operation completed safely.

pages.summary: As an SRE accepting operational ownership of running clusters, this page gives me just enough to understand health signaling and Day-2 management concepts, but critically fails to provide actionable runbooks, thresholds, or remediation steps for any of the failure modes it mentions.
gaps: The heartbeat health check is described (10-minute threshold triggers unhealthy status) but there is no guidance on what to check, where to look, or how to remediate when the agent stops sending heartbeats — no kubectl commands, no log locations, no escalation path.

The page references rolling upgrades, node conditions, cluster profiles, and add-ons like Prometheus and Vault as operational concerns, but provides zero SLO/alerting hooks, no thresholds for node condition failures, and no rollback procedure if a rolling upgrade leaves clusters in a degraded state.
